title: Per-layer working-set forecasting for memory profiles (Llama/Mistral/Qwen, long-context)
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: As we push longer-context use cases across Llama / Mistral / Qwen families, the runtime experiences suboptimal GPU memory utilization when continuous batching mixes sessions with diverse active layer sets. Existing per-variant footprint heuristics are coarse: they over-reserve memory for worst-case sequences or trigger conservative evictions that increase token latency and OOM risk.

Goal: Build a per-layer working-set forecasting subsystem that predicts, at request arrival and per-batch, the expected KV residency (per-layer, per-variant) across the next N tokens and uses those forecasts to drive pre-reservation, targeted prefetching, and tiered eviction thresholds. The forecast should be continuous-batch aware (handle mixed sequence-length batches), cheap to compute, and safe to act on (graceful fallback to current allocator).

Scope and approach:
- Data collection: instrument runtime to record per-request per-layer KV touches and residency lifetimes across representative workloads (webchat, summarization, code completion) for Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Qwen-14B long-context variants. Collect sequence-position-conditioned histograms and mixed-batch co-residency statistics.
- Forecast model: lightweight statistical model (histogram + exponential decay) producing per-layer expected occupancy and percentile estimates (P50/P95) given: model variant, current cumulative token offset, batch composition (list of active sequence lengths), and recent traffic skew. No heavy ML training required initially.
- Allocator integration: map forecasts to three controls: 1) pre-reserve prefix budgets for hot layers, 2) per-layer eviction priority offsets (raise threshold for layers predicted to be needed soon), 3) prefetch budget token counts to warm KV cache asynchronously when latency budget permits.
- Safety: maintain conservative floor and ceiling multipliers; include immediate fallback that disables forecast adjustments if OOMs or latency spikes are observed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reduce OOMs during mixed long-context bursts by >= 60% on bench workloads (vs current baseline).
- Median token latency change <= +5% and 95th percentile latency change <= +10% after enabling forecasts.
- GPU memory fragmentation (measured by free-contiguous-run-size metric) improves or is stable for >= 80% of runs.
- Implementation gated behind feature flag and telemetry to allow rollback.

Deliverables:
- Data pipeline to collect per-layer residency traces and aggregated histograms.
- Forecast library (pure Rust/C++ runtime module) with deterministic outputs and unit tests.
- Allocator shim that applies three controls and config knobs (multipliers, lookahead window, batch-summarizer).
- Eval harness and dashboards (latency, OOMs, memory fragmentation, throughput) and a PRD and design doc.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: quantization-specific kernel changes, cross-GPU sharding logic, and long-term ML-based forecasting. Those can be follow-ups if lightweight approach shows value.
acceptance_criteria: >=60% reduction in OOMs for mixed long-context benchmark suite compared to baseline
Median token latency change <= +5% and P95 latency change <= +10% under 95% traffic mixes
Feature behind runtime feature-flag with automatic rollback on OOM spike
Per-variant forecast unit tests and integration tests in CI
Dashboards showing forecasted vs actual per-layer residency and action logs
implementation_plan: Week 1: Instrument runtime hotspots and collect 2M request samples across three representative workloads (LLama/Mistral/Qwen longctx)
Week 2: Build histogram-based forecast prototype and unit tests; synthetic microbench to validate predictions vs ground truth traces
Week 3: Implement allocator shim and feature-flag hook; run internal canary on dedicated pool with conservative multipliers
Week 4: Expand to mixed-batch production canary, tune multipliers, and add prefetch background worker
Week 5: Run a 48h soak, collect dashboards, produce PR and rollout plan for runtime-1.20
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Forecast drift for novel workloads causing unexpected memory pressure -> Mitigation: conservative multipliers, automatic rollback when OOM rate > baseline threshold
Risk: Extra CPU/host overhead for forecasting harms throughput -> Mitigation: keep forecast computation O(1) per request (histogram lookup + small math); sample traffic to amortize cost
Risk: Prefetching increases token cost or latency -> Mitigation: limit background prefetch to idle cycles and bound budget per second per-GPU
metrics: Forecast accuracy: P50/P95 occupancy error rate
notes: Related research: evaluated simple exponential-decay forecasters vs small LSTM; lightweight forecasters gave 80-90% of accuracy at <5% CPU overhead in local sims
We must coordinate with Dedicated infra to test reserved-capacity behavior (burst vs steady) as pre-reservation semantics interact with autoscaling
Design reviewed with Storage/Allocator team 2025-01-22; follow-up: add a telemetry event schema for forecast actions
